reason: The text depicts King Josiah's people as supportive and cooperative with his leadership. The narrative shows the people readily gathering when summoned by the king (all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem), participating actively in the covenant ceremony he led, and standing together in the covenant ('וַיַּעֲמֹד כָּל־ הָעָם בַּבְּרִֽית' - 'all the people stood in the covenant'). The people of the land also took decisive action to anoint his successor after his death. Throughout the passage, there is no evidence of popular antagonism or resistance to Josiah; rather, the account demonstrates the people's willing participation in his religious reforms and covenant commitment.
